q_emergency_triage.title: Primary Laptop Symptom
q_emergency_triage.question: What is the primary issue you are facing with your laptop right now?
q_emergency_triage.why: Identifies the core hardware/software failure domain to immediately eliminate unrelated diagnostic branches.

options.label: Completely dead, won't turn on, or charging problems
Screen is black, flickering, distorted, or has lines
Overheating, screaming fans, or shutting down under load
Boot loop, Blue Screen (BSOD), or 'No Boot Device' error
Random freezing, beep codes, or memory crashes
Keyboard, trackpad, USB ports, sound, or Wi-Fi broken

q_power_state.title: Power-On Response
q_power_state.question: When pressing the power button, does the laptop show ANY signs of life (fan spin, LEDs, keyboard light, sound)?
q_power_state.why: Differentiates between complete mother-rail/power delivery failure and partial POST initialization.

options.label: Zero signs of life (completely unresponsive)
options.defect_description: Laptop fails to initiate power rails (No POST, No LEDs)

options.label: Turns on normally and boots
Powers on for 1-3 seconds, then immediately shuts off
options.defect_description: Power loop / Short circuit protection trigger

leaf_diagnosis.title: Motherboard Short Circuit or Power Rail Trip
leaf_diagnosis.issue: The power management IC (PMIC) is detecting an over-current condition or shorted capacitor/MOSFET on a secondary rail (3.3V/5V/VCore), triggering immediate emergency shutdown.
remediation: Perform a hard EC reset: Disconnect charger, hold power button down for 45 seconds.
If internal battery is accessible, disconnect battery and run on AC adapter only.
Inspect USB ports for physically bent or bridged metal pins causing 5V shorts.
If behavior persists, board-level repair or motherboard replacement is required.

q_charger_led.title: AC Adapter / Charging Port LED
q_charger_led.question: When the charger is plugged in, does the charging indicator LED on the laptop or the charger turn on?
q_charger_led.why: Determines whether DC voltage is successfully reaching the DC-in jack and charging circuit.

options.label: No LED lights up anywhere
options.defect_description: No DC input detected; dead AC adapter or broken DC jack

leaf_diagnosis.title: Faulty AC Adapter or Broken DC-In Power Jack
leaf_diagnosis.issue: No electrical potential is reaching the charging circuit. The charger brick has failed, the wall outlet is dead, or the physical center pin / soldered DC-in jack is cracked.
remediation: Test the wall outlet with a known working lamp or phone charger.
Test with an alternate OEM charger with matching voltage and amperage rating.
Check the DC barrel / Type-C cable for frayed wires or bent internal pins.
Replace the modular DC-in harness cable if the laptop uses a cable-style jack.

options.label: Yes, charging LED turns on (solid white/amber)
LED blinks repeatedly in a distinct color/number pattern
options.defect_description: OEM diagnostic blink code indicating hardware failure

leaf_diagnosis.title: OEM Diagnostic Hardware Error Code
leaf_diagnosis.issue: Modern laptops (Dell, HP, Lenovo) flash power/battery LEDs to signal specific board errors (e.g. 2 amber + 3 white = No RAM detected, 3 amber + 5 white = Power rail failure).
remediation: Count the exact sequence of blinks (e.g., number of amber vs white blinks).
Look up the diagnostic code in your laptop manufacturer's service manual.
Reseat memory modules if the blink code points to memory fault.
Perform a CMOS/RTC battery clear.

q_power_button_feel.title: Power Button Mechanics
q_power_button_feel.question: Does the power button feel physically clicky and intact, or is it recessed/integrated into the keyboard?
q_power_button_feel.why: Many modern laptops integrate the power button into the keyboard matrix; a spilled beverage or severed ribbon cable disables the power trigger.

options.label: Button clicks normally and powers on laptop reliably
Button clicks normally, but laptop still will not turn on
options.defect_description: Internal Embedded Controller (EC) or BIOS failure

leaf_diagnosis.title: Dead Motherboard / Failed Embedded Controller (EC)
leaf_diagnosis.issue: The laptop receives standby 19V and 3.3V, but the Embedded Controller fails to trigger the system power-on sequence (`PCH_PWR_EN` / `RSMRST#`).
remediation: Unplug charger and battery, hold power button 60 seconds to drain capacitors.
Disconnect the coin-cell CMOS battery for 15 minutes to reset the BIOS state.
Reflash the BIOS chip using a hardware programmer (CH341A) or send for board diagnosis.

options.label: Button is stuck, mushy, or damaged from liquid spill
options.defect_description: Damaged power switch / keyboard power key failure

leaf_diagnosis.title: Defective Power Button or Keyboard Assembly
leaf_diagnosis.issue: The physical tactile micro-switch is corroded, broken, or the keyboard membrane trace for the power button has disconnected.
remediation: Replace the small power button sub-board or the top-case keyboard assembly.
If keyboard-integrated, test by bridging the power pins on the motherboard power connector.

q_charging_behavior.title: Battery Charging Status
q_charging_behavior.question: In the OS, does the battery status say 'Plugged in, charging' and actually increase in percentage?
q_charging_behavior.why: Identifies battery cell degradation, charging MOSFET failures, and SMBus battery communication errors.

options.label: Charges normally to 100%
Says 'Plugged in, not charging' or percentage stays frozen
options.defect_description: Battery firmware lockout or charging circuit failure

leaf_diagnosis.title: Battery Charging Lockout or Degraded Cells
leaf_diagnosis.issue: The battery BMS (Battery Management System) has locked out charging due to cell imbalance, or the Microsoft ACPI-Compliant Control Method Battery driver is corrupted.
remediation: Open Device Manager -> Batteries -> Uninstall 'Microsoft ACPI-Compliant Control Method Battery' -> Restart.
Check battery health report in terminal (`powercfg /batteryreport` on Windows or `upower` on Linux).
Check if manufacturer battery conservation mode (e.g. Lenovo Vantage 60% cap) is active.

options.label: Laptop instantly dies the exact millisecond the AC charger is unplugged
options.defect_description: Dead battery pack or blown battery discharge fuse

leaf_diagnosis.title: Dead Internal Battery Pack
leaf_diagnosis.issue: The internal battery cells have zero voltage capacity, a blown thermal fuse on the BMS, or the battery connector is disconnected.
remediation: Replace internal battery pack with a genuine OEM replacement.
Inspect battery connector pins for corrosion or bent terminals.

q_battery_discharge.title: Battery Runtime & Life
q_battery_discharge.question: How long does the battery last on a full charge under typical web browsing / office use?
q_battery_discharge.why: Quantifies wear level and real-world degradation of lithium-ion cells.

options.label: 4+ hours of healthy backup
2 to 3 hours (moderate wear)
Less than 45 minutes / sudden drops from 40% to 5%
options.defect_description: Severe battery wear (>60% capacity loss)

q_battery_bulge.title: Physical Battery Swelling / Trackpad Lifting
q_battery_bulge.question: Is the trackpad lifting, palm rest bowing upwards, or bottom chassis seam splitting?
q_battery_bulge.why: Swollen lithium pouches are a fire hazard and physically destroy touchpads and chassis.

options.label: No swelling, chassis and trackpad are completely flat
YES! Trackpad is pushed up or chassis bottom is bulging
options.defect_description: Critically swollen lithium-ion battery pack (FIRE HAZARD)

leaf_diagnosis.title: DANGEROUS: Swollen Lithium-Ion Battery
leaf_diagnosis.issue: Electrolyte gas buildup inside lithium pouches due to age, heat, or internal shorting. Poses an imminent thermal runaway/fire risk and will crack the trackpad glass.
remediation: STOP using and STOP charging the laptop immediately.
Safely power down the device.
Carefully unscrew bottom cover and remove swollen battery pack; dispose at certified e-waste facility.
DO NOT puncture, bend, or crush the battery.

q_usbc_charging.title: USB-C Power Delivery Recognition
q_usbc_charging.question: If your laptop supports USB-C charging, does it negotiate charging on all USB-C PD ports?
q_usbc_charging.why: Validates USB Type-C Power Delivery controller chips (TI / Cypress / Parade) and ESD protection diodes.

options.label: Charges properly via USB-C (or uses traditional DC barrel jack)
Shows 'Slow charger' warning or port is loose/unresponsive
options.defect_description: USB-C PD CC-line failure or loose daughterboard port

q_display_illumination.title: Display Power & Illumination
q_display_illumination.question: When the laptop is on, does the screen light up at all, or is it completely pitch black?
q_display_illumination.why: Separates backlight circuit / panel defects from GPU rendering failures.

options.label: Screen lights up and displays an image or logo
Screen is completely black (no backlight glow)
options.defect_description: Black screen with laptop powered on

q_flashlight_test.title: Flashlight Backlight Test
q_flashlight_test.question: If you shine your smartphone flashlight directly onto the black screen at an angle, can you faintly see desktop icons or text?
q_flashlight_test.why: If faint image is visible, the LCD panel and GPU work fine, but the LED backlight fuse or inverter has blown.

options.label: Not Applicable (Screen displays normally with backlight)
Yes! I can faintly see windows/text under the bright flashlight
options.defect_description: Blown motherboard backlight fuse or dead screen LED strip

leaf_diagnosis.title: Blown Screen Backlight Fuse / Circuit
leaf_diagnosis.issue: The LCD panel is receiving video data from the GPU, but the 19V LED backlight power circuit (often protected by a 0402 SMD fuse near the eDP connector) has blown.
remediation: Often caused by plugging in or unplugging the screen ribbon cable while battery was connected.
Test continuity of the backlight SMD fuse on the motherboard with a multimeter.
If fuse is intact, replace the LCD panel or the eDP cable.

options.label: No, nothing at all is visible even under direct flashlight
options.defect_description: No video signal generated (RAM/GPU/eDP cable failure)

q_external_monitor.title: External Monitor / TV Connection
q_external_monitor.question: When you plug the laptop into an external monitor or TV via HDMI / Type-C, does an image appear on the external screen?
q_external_monitor.why: Pinpoints whether the GPU is alive and outputting frames, isolating the issue to the internal panel/cable vs. system board.

options.label: Not Applicable (Internal screen working fine)
YES! External monitor shows full normal desktop
options.defect_description: Defective internal LCD screen or damaged eDP display ribbon cable

leaf_diagnosis.title: Defective Laptop LCD Screen or Damaged eDP Cable
leaf_diagnosis.issue: The CPU/GPU and operating system are running smoothly, but the internal eDP (embedded DisplayPort) ribbon cable is pinched in the hinge or the LCD controller is dead.
remediation: Open bottom panel and verify internal display ribbon cable is securely seated in the motherboard latch.
Inspect ribbon cable for wear or crimping near the hinge.
Replace the internal LCD screen panel (match model number on back of panel).

options.label: NO, external monitor also says 'No Signal'
options.defect_description: System fails POST / No video signal generated from GPU/RAM

q_screen_flicker.title: Hinge Movement & Screen Flicker
q_screen_flicker.question: Does the screen flicker, go black, or show horizontal glitch lines when you physically tilt the laptop lid back and forth?
q_screen_flicker.why: Movement-correlated distortion is the hallmark signature of a physically pinched or frayed eDP video cable inside the clutch hinge.

options.label: Screen is completely stable at all angles
Yes, moving the lid causes screen blinking or visual tears
options.defect_description: Frayed or loose eDP video ribbon cable passing through hinge

leaf_diagnosis.title: Frayed or Pinched eDP Display Ribbon Cable
leaf_diagnosis.issue: Repeated opening and closing of the laptop lid has worn down the microscopic copper conductors inside the video ribbon harness passing through the hinge.
remediation: Order a replacement eDP video cable matching your exact laptop model.
Remove screen bezel and bottom chassis to route and install the new harness.
Verify hinge tension is not overly tight.

q_gpu_artifacts.title: Graphical Artifacts & Pixel Glitches
q_gpu_artifacts.question: Do you see colored blocks, pink/green lines, checkerboard patterns, or driver crashing during video playback or games?
q_gpu_artifacts.why: Detects failing VRAM chips, cold solder joints under the GPU BGA, or failing display drivers.

options.label: Image is clean with zero visual artifacts
Yes, colored lines, checkerboards, or direct driver timeout crashes
options.defect_description: GPU VRAM memory degradation or failing BGA solder balls

leaf_diagnosis.title: Failing Dedicated GPU or VRAM Memory Degradation
leaf_diagnosis.issue: Thermal cycling has cracked microscopic solder balls beneath the dedicated GPU (Nvidia/AMD) or VRAM chips, causing corrupted framebuffers and TDR crashes.
remediation: Perform a clean GPU driver reinstall using Display Driver Uninstaller (DDU) in Safe Mode.
Underclock GPU core and memory clocks by 100MHz using MSI Afterburner to test stability.
If artifacts persist in BIOS, hardware BGA reballing or board replacement is required.

q_dead_pixels.title: Dead Pixels & Panel Bleed
q_dead_pixels.question: Are there permanent colored dots (stuck pixels), black spots, or severe backlight bleeding in corners?
q_dead_pixels.why: Physical panel quality check for pre-purchase inspection.

options.label: Panel is pristine, no stuck pixels or severe bleed
1-3 dead pixels or minor backlight bleed (cosmetic)
Permanent vertical colored lines or ink-like black blotches
options.defect_description: Physically damaged LCD substrate / cracked panel

q_fan_noise.title: Cooling Fan Sound & Acoustics
q_fan_noise.question: What does the cooling fan sound like when spinning?
q_fan_noise.why: Identifies worn fan sleeve bearings, off-balance blades, or physical cable obstructions.

options.label: Smooth airflow whoosh with no weird noises
Rattling, buzzing, grinding, or high-pitched squeak
options.defect_description: Worn fan sleeve bearings or broken fan blade

leaf_diagnosis.title: Worn Cooling Fan Bearing or Blade Obstruction
leaf_diagnosis.issue: The fluid dynamic or sleeve bearing inside the brushless fan motor has dried out, causing vibration, acoustic rattle, and reduced RPM cooling performance.
remediation: Open bottom panel and inspect fan for hair, debris, or loose cables rubbing against blades.
Clean with compressed air while holding the fan blades still (prevent back-EMF).
Replace the cooling fan assembly (readily available OEM part for $15–$30).

options.label: Fan NEVER spins at all, even when laptop gets blistering hot
options.defect_description: Dead cooling fan motor or blown 5V fan header circuit

leaf_diagnosis.title: Seized Fan Motor or Fan Header Failure
leaf_diagnosis.issue: Zero active cooling is operating. The laptop will thermal-throttle down to un-usable speeds and shut down violently to prevent CPU silicon destruction.
remediation: Check if fan connector is disconnected from the motherboard.
Replace the defective fan unit immediately.
Do not use laptop under load until fan is repaired.

q_fan_speed_idle.title: Fan Behavior at Idle
q_fan_speed_idle.question: When sitting on the desktop with no programs open, are the fans roaring at 100% full speed continuously?
q_fan_speed_idle.why: Flags runaway background processes, dried thermal paste, or faulty temperature sensor readings.

options.label: Quiet or completely silent at idle
Fans scream at 100% nonstop, even when cold or idling
options.defect_description: Thermal paste pump-out or background crypto miner/runaway process

q_chassis_heat.title: Bottom Chassis Temperature
q_chassis_heat.question: Does the bottom chassis or keyboard deck get uncomfortably or dangerously hot to the touch during use?
q_chassis_heat.why: Indicates clogged heatsink fin stacks or dried out thermal interface material.

options.label: Mildly warm, comfortable on lap
Scorching hot (cannot touch bottom panel for more than 5 seconds)
options.defect_description: Severe heat accumulation / thermal bottleneck

q_thermal_shutdown.title: Thermal Emergency Power Cutoff
q_thermal_shutdown.question: Does the laptop abruptly shut off with zero warning after 15-30 minutes of gaming, video editing, or heavy load?
q_thermal_shutdown.why: CPU/GPU thermal junction limit (PROCHOT at ~100°C) triggering emergency hardware shutdown to prevent silicon damage.

options.label: Never shuts down abruptly during heavy tasks
Yes, consistently powers off after gaming or heavy stress
options.defect_description: Severe thermal junction trip (CPU/GPU hitting 105°C)

leaf_diagnosis.title: Severe Thermal Overheating (Dried Paste / Clogged Heatsink)
leaf_diagnosis.issue: A 'dust felt' blanket has formed between the fan impeller and the copper heatsink radiator fins, or the factory thermal paste has dried into a chalky insulator, trapping 100°C+ heat on the die.
remediation: Remove heatsink, scrape off hardened thermal paste using 99% isopropyl alcohol.
Apply high-viscosity thermal paste (e.g., Honeywell PTM7950 or Arctic MX-6).
Blow compressed air through heatsink exhaust radiator fins to dislodge dust blankets.
Ensure all thermal pads on VRMs and VRAM make proper contact.

q_boot_outcome.title: Bootloader & OS Startup
q_boot_outcome.question: What happens on screen immediately after the manufacturer logo appears?
q_boot_outcome.why: Isolates storage drive hardware recognition from OS bootloader corruption and hardware crashes.

options.label: Boots straight to Windows/Linux desktop normally
Shows 'No Bootable Device Found' or boots directly to BIOS
options.defect_description: Storage drive unreadable or corrupted EFI boot partition

leaf_diagnosis.title: Unrecognized Storage Drive or Corrupted EFI Bootloader
leaf_diagnosis.issue: The motherboard firmware cannot detect a readable bootable partition. Either the NVMe M.2 / SATA SSD has disconnected/died, or the UEFI EFI partition is wiped.
remediation: Enter BIOS (press F2 / Del / F12 on boot) and verify if the SSD model name is listed in the storage menu.
If SSD is listed in BIOS: Boot from a USB installer and run `bootrec /fixboot` and `bcdboot` to rebuild EFI.
If SSD is NOT listed in BIOS: Reseat the M.2 SSD in its slot; if still missing, SSD controller has died.

options.label: Gets stuck on an endless spinning loading wheel or automatic repair loop
options.defect_description: Corrupted OS system files or failing SSD bad blocks

leaf_diagnosis.title: Corrupted Operating System or Filesystem Bad Blocks
leaf_diagnosis.issue: Core system files (e.g. `ntoskrnl.exe`, system registry hive) failed integrity check during kernel load.
remediation: Boot into Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) -> Advanced Options -> Startup Repair.
Open Command Prompt in WinRE and run `chkdsk C: /f /r` and `sfc /scannow`.
If automatic repair fails repeatedly, perform a clean OS reinstallation.

q_bsod_crashes.title: Blue Screen (BSOD) / Kernel Panic
q_bsod_crashes.question: Does the laptop encounter Blue Screens of Death (BSOD), kernel panics, or sudden reboots?
q_bsod_crashes.why: Distinguishes between stable system operation and kernel-level hardware driver/hardware faults.

options.label: Never encounters Blue Screens (rock stable)
Frequent BSODs with random stop codes (CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED, KERNEL_DATA_INPAGE_ERROR)
options.defect_description: System instability / RAM or SSD page fault crash

leaf_diagnosis.title: Failing Storage Drive or Corrupt Pagefile (Kernel Data Inpage Error)
leaf_diagnosis.issue: Stop codes like `KERNEL_DATA_INPAGE_ERROR` or `UNEXPECTED_STORE_EXCEPTION` occur when the OS attempts to read memory pages cached on the SSD, but the storage drive drops offline momentarily.
remediation: Check drive health using CrystalDiskInfo or smartctl.
Reseat NVMe SSD and check for thermal throttling on SSD controller.
Update SSD firmware from manufacturer utility (Samsung Magician, Crucial Executive, etc.).

q_drive_sounds.title: Storage Acoustic Clicking / Beeping
q_drive_sounds.question: Do you hear rhythmic mechanical clicking, scratching, or ticking sounds coming from the palm rest area?
q_drive_sounds.why: Mechanical click of death indicates head-crash on mechanical HDD; SSDs are purely silent.

options.label: Completely silent (Solid State / NVMe drive)
Repetitive mechanical clicking or scratching sounds
options.defect_description: Mechanical HDD head failure ('Click of Death')

leaf_diagnosis.title: Imminent Mechanical Hard Drive Failure (Click of Death)
leaf_diagnosis.issue: The read/write heads of a mechanical hard disk are failing to find track zero and colliding against the actuator park stopper. Total data loss is imminent.
remediation: BACK UP CRITICAL DATA IMMEDIATELY before turning the laptop off.
Do not run intensive defragmentation or disk repair scans.
Replace the failing mechanical HDD with a modern 2.5" SATA SSD or M.2 NVMe SSD.

q_boot_speed.title: Boot Time Performance
q_boot_speed.question: How long does it take from pressing the power button to reaching a responsive desktop?
q_boot_speed.why: Identifies slow mechanical hard drives or failing SSD NAND flash controller degradation.

options.label: Under 20 seconds (Fast NVMe SSD speed)
20 to 60 seconds (Acceptable SATA speed)
Over 2 minutes with 100% disk usage in Task Manager
options.defect_description: Severe storage IOPS bottleneck (Slow 5400RPM HDD or degraded SSD)

q_post_beeps.title: POST Beep Codes / Diagnostic Sequences
q_post_beeps.question: Does the laptop emit audible beeps (e.g. 1-3-3-1 or continuous beeps) upon power-up?
q_post_beeps.why: Audible BIOS beeps are standardized hardware diagnostic alerts generated before the display subsystem initializes.

options.label: No error beeps (normal startup)
Yes, rhythmic beep sequences or siren tones play on power-up
options.defect_description: POST memory / motherboard hardware diagnostic beep code

leaf_diagnosis.title: POST Hardware Beep Code (RAM Initialization Failure)
leaf_diagnosis.issue: The BIOS power-on self-test failed during base 64K memory or SPD reading. Most commonly caused by oxidized RAM golden fingers or loose SO-DIMM latch.
remediation: Power off, remove battery/charger, open bottom cover.
Remove RAM modules, clean golden contacts gently with an eraser and isopropyl alcohol.
Test modules one stick at a time in alternate slots to identify whether a module or a slot is dead.

q_ram_recognized.title: Installed vs Usable RAM Capacity
q_ram_recognized.question: In Windows 'About PC' or Linux `free -h`, is all installed physical RAM recognized and usable?
q_ram_recognized.why: Detects dead RAM channels, faulty memory mapping, or disabled integrated memory banks.

options.label: All installed RAM is recognized (e.g., full 16GB usable)
Only half is recognized (e.g., 16GB installed but only 8GB shown)
options.defect_description: Unrecognized memory channel or dead secondary RAM stick

leaf_diagnosis.title: Unrecognized Memory Stick or Dead RAM Slot
leaf_diagnosis.issue: One of the memory modules has failed to train during BIOS POST, or the second memory channel has broken BGA traces to the CPU memory controller.
remediation: Reseat the unrecognized RAM module firmly into its slot until latches click.
Swap sticks between slots: if the problem follows the stick, replace the RAM stick; if it stays in the slot, slot is dead.

q_random_freezing.title: Sudden System Freezing & Lockups
q_random_freezing.question: Does the laptop randomly freeze completely (mouse cursor completely frozen, requiring hard power button hold)?
q_random_freezing.why: Unresponsive hard locks point to RAM bit-flips, unstable VRM voltages, or SSD controller timeouts.

options.label: System runs smoothly without hard freezes
Frequent hard freezes requiring holding the power button
options.defect_description: Hardware instability / Memory bit-flips under load

leaf_diagnosis.title: RAM Memory Instability or Unstable CPU C-States
leaf_diagnosis.issue: Memory bit errors (flipping 1s to 0s) or aggressive CPU low-power C-states causing kernel thread deadlocks.
remediation: Run Windows Memory Diagnostic (`mdsched.exe`) or MemTest86 overnight.
Disable Intel SpeedStep or AMD Cool'n'Quiet temporarily in BIOS to test power state stability.
Replace faulty RAM module if MemTest reports any memory errors.

q_keyboard_keys.title: Keyboard Key Functionality
q_keyboard_keys.question: Are all keyboard keys typing reliably, or are some keys unresponsive, stuck, or typing phantom letters?
q_keyboard_keys.why: Physical inspection of membrane matrix traces and beverage spill damage.

options.label: Every key works crisply and accurately
Several keys are completely dead or spamming repeated letters
options.defect_description: Damaged keyboard membrane or broken scissor switches

leaf_diagnosis.title: Failed Keyboard Membrane Matrix (Spill / Trace Corrosion)
leaf_diagnosis.issue: The microscopic conductive silver traces on the flexible keyboard membrane have oxidized from moisture, severing an entire matrix row or column of keys.
remediation: Test in an online keyboard tester to see if dead keys share a specific electrical row.
Clean under keys with compressed air and contact cleaner.
Replace the internal keyboard or upper palm rest assembly.

q_keyboard_backlight.title: Keyboard Backlighting
q_keyboard_backlight.question: Does the keyboard backlight turn on and adjust brightness via the function keys?
q_keyboard_backlight.why: Validates separate keyboard LED ribbon cable and ambient lighting controllers.

options.label: Backlight works properly (or laptop does not have a backlit keyboard)
Backlit keyboard is dark and won't turn on
options.defect_description: Disconnected keyboard backlight ribbon cable

q_trackpad_click.title: Trackpad Physical Click & Surface
q_trackpad_click.question: Does the trackpad have a crisp tactile click, and does the pointer glide smoothly without jumping?
q_trackpad_click.why: Detects battery swelling underneath trackpad, worn dome switches, or grounding grounding issues.

options.label: Smooth tracking with crisp, responsive clicks
Click is stiff/jammed, or cursor jumps wildly and phantom clicks
options.defect_description: Jammed trackpad dome switch, grounding noise, or battery swelling

leaf_diagnosis.title: Jammed Trackpad Mechanism or Battery Pressure
leaf_diagnosis.issue: A swelling battery directly beneath the touchpad is pressing the tactile switch permanently closed, or the grounding spring has lost contact with the chassis.
remediation: Inspect bottom of laptop to confirm battery is not swollen.
Adjust the central clicker tension set-screw on the bottom of the trackpad bracket.
Clean around trackpad edges to dislodge dirt or sticky residue.

q_usb_ports.title: USB Type-A Port Integrity
q_usb_ports.question: Do all USB Type-A ports recognize flash drives and power peripherals reliably without wiggling?
q_usb_ports.why: Detects physically broken plastic tongues, bent 5V pins, or blown port polyfuses.

options.label: All USB-A ports work securely
One or more USB ports are physically loose or disconnected
options.defect_description: Desoldered or physically broken USB-A port

q_webcam_mic.title: Webcam & Microphone
q_webcam_mic.question: When opening the Camera app, does the webcam display clear video and does the mic capture clear audio?
q_webcam_mic.why: Validates USB/MIPI video lines routed through the display lid and physical privacy shutters.

options.label: Both webcam and microphone function clearly
Camera says 'No Camera Found' or video is distorted/pitch black
options.defect_description: Severed webcam ribbon harness in display bezel

q_wifi_reception.title: Wi-Fi Connectivity & Signal Range
q_wifi_reception.question: Does the laptop maintain strong Wi-Fi connections, or does signal drop out a few rooms away?
q_wifi_reception.why: Detects disconnected U.FL coaxial antenna leads or failing M.2 WLAN card (Intel/Realtek/MediaTek).

options.label: Strong signal with fast, stable speeds
Wi-Fi adapter completely disappears or signal only works next to router
options.defect_description: Disconnected internal antenna lead or defective M.2 Wi-Fi card

leaf_diagnosis.title: Disconnected Antenna Leads or Failing M.2 Wi-Fi Card
leaf_diagnosis.issue: The micro-coaxial antenna leads (Main/Aux) have popped off the M.2 Wi-Fi card, or the PCIe Wi-Fi card has suffered a thermal failure.
remediation: Open bottom cover and verify both black/white antenna snap-connectors are firmly seated onto the M.2 card.
Ensure Intel/Realtek WLAN drivers are updated.
Replace M.2 Wi-Fi card with a high-performance Intel AX210 card ($20).

q_bluetooth_pairing.title: Bluetooth Subsystem
q_bluetooth_pairing.question: Does Bluetooth turn on, discover devices, and stream audio without stuttering?
q_bluetooth_pairing.why: Validates USB subsystem bus handling Bluetooth on combo WLAN cards.

options.label: Bluetooth pairs and works without issue
Bluetooth option is completely missing from settings
options.defect_description: Disabled Bluetooth USB host controller or driver fault

q_speakers_clarity.title: Internal Speakers Acoustic Quality
q_speakers_clarity.question: Do the internal laptop speakers produce clean stereo sound, or do they crackle, buzz, or remain completely silent?
q_speakers_clarity.why: Detects torn speaker paper cones, metal shavings stuck to speaker magnets, or failed audio codecs.

options.label: Clean stereo sound from both left and right speakers
Horrible buzzing, crackling distortion, or one side dead
options.defect_description: Torn speaker diaphragm or metal debris on magnetic voice coil

options.label: Completely silent despite audio playing in OS
options.defect_description: Disconnected internal speaker harness or audio amplifier IC fault

q_headphone_jack.title: 3.5mm Headphone / Combo Audio Jack
q_headphone_jack.question: When plugging in wired headphones, does the laptop detect them immediately and route sound cleanly?
q_headphone_jack.why: Checks mechanical sense pins inside the audio jack socket.

options.label: Headphone audio routes immediately and cleanly
Loose connection, static noise on movement, or broken off tip inside
options.defect_description: Damaged internal 3.5mm audio jack sense pin

q_chassis_hinges.title: Hinge Rigidity & Chassis Seam Integrity
q_chassis_hinges.question: Are the display hinges firm and sturdy, or are brass screw mounts cracked out of the plastic palm rest?
q_chassis_hinges.why: Cracked hinge brass standoffs are the #1 physical failure mode on mid-range laptops (HP 15, Dell Inspiron, Lenovo IdeaPad).

options.label: Hinges are smooth, sturdy, and chassis seams are tight
Hinge is wobbling, stiff, or plastic chassis splits open when opening the lid
options.defect_description: Ruptured brass standoff nuts inside plastic palm rest / lid assembly

leaf_diagnosis.title: Ruptured Display Hinge Brass Standoffs
leaf_diagnosis.issue: Excessive factory hinge torque has sheared the heat-set brass threaded nuts straight out of the plastic top-cover or screen back-cover. Continuing to force it will shatter the LCD screen and sever the video cable.
remediation: Loosen the hinge tension nut slightly (1/8 turn) to reduce mechanical torque.
Re-anchor brass standoffs using high-strength structural epoxy (e.g. JB Weld PlasticWeld) or replace top cover.
Do not force lid open or closed until repaired.

q_cmos_battery.title: System Time & CMOS Battery
q_cmos_battery.question: Does the laptop system time/date reset to Jan 1, 2015 or prompt with 'Time-of-day clock stopped' every time power is lost?
q_cmos_battery.why: Tests the condition of the RTC 3V coin-cell (CR2032 or heat-shrink 2-pin lithium battery).

options.label: Time and date stay synchronized correctly
Time resets every restart or BIOS prompts 'CMOS Checksum Error'
options.defect_description: Exhausted 3V RTC / CMOS coin cell battery

leaf_diagnosis.title: Dead CMOS / Real-Time Clock (RTC) Battery
leaf_diagnosis.issue: The miniature coin-cell battery powering the motherboard's RTC chip and non-volatile BIOS memory has dropped below 2.5V.
remediation: Locate the CR2032 coin cell on the motherboard (often wrapped in yellow or black shrink tubing with a 2-pin molex header).
Replace with a fresh 3V CR2032 coin cell.
Re-enter BIOS and set correct date, time, and boot order.

q_liquid_spill.title: Liquid Exposure History
q_liquid_spill.question: Has the laptop suffered any liquid spill (water, coffee, soda) or lived in a high-humidity environment?
q_liquid_spill.why: Liquid damage creates creeping galvanic corrosion that bridges power rails weeks or months after the incident.

options.label: Zero liquid contact; clean interior history
Yes, liquid was spilled onto keyboard or ports
options.defect_description: Liquid ingress with progressive copper corrosion

leaf_diagnosis.title: Liquid Ingress & Active Motherboard Corrosion
leaf_diagnosis.issue: Moisture combined with active electrical current causes rapid electrolytic corrosion, eating copper traces and shorting SMD capacitors under BGAs.
remediation: DISCONNECT battery and charger immediately; DO NOT try to power on.
DO NOT place in rice (rice dust enters fans and traps moisture).
Disassemble completely, inspect Liquid Contact Indicators (LCIs).
Clean all green/white corrosion under a microscope using 99% isopropyl alcohol and ultrasonic cleaner.

q_tpm_secure_boot.title: TPM 2.0 & Secure Boot Status
q_tpm_secure_boot.question: Does Windows 11 report 'TPM not detected' or fail to boot due to Secure Boot signature violations?
q_tpm_secure_boot.why: Verifies hardware platform trust technology (fTPM / dTPM) required by modern operating systems.

options.label: TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot are operational
TPM is missing in Device Manager or Secure Boot errors on boot
options.defect_description: Firmware TPM disabled or corrupted Platform Trust Technology

leaf_diagnosis.title: Disabled or Corrupted TPM / Platform Trust Module
leaf_diagnosis.issue: The Intel PTT (Platform Trust Technology) or AMD fTPM has become corrupted in the SPI flash chip or disabled in BIOS.
remediation: Enter BIOS -> Security -> Enable Intel PTT / AMD fTPM and clear TPM keys.
Update laptop BIOS to the latest version to apply firmware TPM fixes.
Ensure UEFI boot mode is enabled rather than Legacy CSM.

q_bios_password.title: BIOS / Supervisor Lock
q_bios_password.question: Is the BIOS setup or boot process locked behind an unknown master password?
q_bios_password.why: Critical pre-purchase check; corporate locked laptops (Computrace / Supervisor lock) prevent boot drive modifications.

options.label: BIOS is fully accessible with no passwords
BIOS prompts for password and locks out changes
options.defect_description: Active BIOS supervisor password / Enterprise lock

leaf_diagnosis.title: BIOS Supervisor Lock / Enterprise Security Lock
leaf_diagnosis.issue: A password is stored in non-volatile EEPROM/EC memory. On modern business laptops, pulling the CMOS battery will NOT clear this password.
remediation: If purchased used, request the master password from the seller or previous IT department.
Check for master backdoor hash codes at bios-pw.org.
May require flashing a clean, unprovisioned BIOS dump to the SPI ROM using a programmer.

q_bitlocker_recovery.title: BitLocker Recovery Prompts
q_bitlocker_recovery.question: Does Windows prompt for a 48-digit BitLocker recovery key on startup?
q_bitlocker_recovery.why: Indicates PCR bank checksum changes caused by BIOS updates or TPM communication failure.

options.label: Never prompts for BitLocker recovery keys
Prompts for BitLocker key unexpectedly
options.defect_description: BitLocker PCR validation failure or wiped TPM state

leaf_diagnosis.title: BitLocker Integrity Check Triggered
leaf_diagnosis.issue: The TPM detected a hardware modification, BIOS revision change, or boot order alteration that altered the Platform Configuration Registers (PCR).
remediation: Log into your Microsoft Account at https://account.microsoft.com/devices/recoverykey to retrieve the 48-digit key.
Suspend BitLocker in Windows before performing any future BIOS updates.
Re-bind PCR banks in elevated terminal: `manage-bde -protectors -delete C: -type TPM` then `manage-bde -protectors -add C: -tpm`.

q_smart_health.title: SSD S.M.A.R.T. Health Status
q_smart_health.question: Do disk utilities (CrystalDiskInfo / smartctl) show 'Caution' or report bad reallocated sectors / percentage used wear > 90%?
q_smart_health.why: Early warning indicator before complete catastrophic NAND flash failure.

options.label: Status is 'Good' (100% or low wear, 0 bad sectors)
Status shows 'Caution' or has reallocated sectors
options.defect_description: Degraded SSD NAND endurance or bad sector reallocations

leaf_diagnosis.title: Degraded Storage Drive (Failing S.M.A.R.T. Health)
leaf_diagnosis.issue: The drive's spare reserve flash blocks are running out. Bad blocks can no longer be transparently remapped, leading to data corruption.
remediation: Immediately clone or back up your entire drive to external storage.
Replace the SSD with a new NVMe PCIe Gen 4 SSD.
Do not trust the drive with critical unbacked-up data.

q_ram_speed_xmp.title: RAM Speed & JEDEC Profile
q_ram_speed_xmp.question: In Task Manager -> Performance -> Memory, is RAM running at its rated speed (e.g. 3200MHz / 4800MHz / 5600MHz)?
q_ram_speed_xmp.why: Checks if mismatched RAM modules forced motherboard into fallback 2133MHz / 2400MHz baseline.

options.label: Running at rated maximum speed
Downclocked to base JEDEC speed (e.g. 2133MHz or 2400MHz)

q_coil_whine.title: Inductor Coil Whine
q_coil_whine.question: Do you hear a faint high-pitched electrical hissing, chirping, or buzzing from the keyboard area when moving the mouse or playing games?
q_coil_whine.why: Physical vibration of copper wire coils inside surface-mount ferrite power inductors.

options.label: Completely quiet electrical rails
Yes, audible high-pitched buzzing under GPU/CPU load
options.defect_description: Harmless acoustic vibration of motherboard VRM power inductors

leaf_diagnosis.title: Motherboard VRM Inductor Coil Whine
leaf_diagnosis.issue: High frequency switching current flowing through the CPU/GPU VRM inductors creates a magnetic field that physically vibrates the internal coils at audible audio frequencies.
remediation: This is an acoustic nuisance but is 100% harmless to hardware life.
Disabling aggressive C-states (C1E) in BIOS can reduce pitch fluctuations.
Capping framerates in games eliminates extreme GPU coil whine spikes.

q_touchscreen_ghost.title: Touchscreen Accuracy & Ghost Touches
q_touchscreen_ghost.question: If your laptop has a touchscreen, does it experience 'ghost touches' (phantom circles clicking automatically)?
q_touchscreen_ghost.why: Digitizer glass micro-fractures or electrostatic ground leakage across the touch matrix.

options.label: Accurate tracking (or non-touch laptop)
Phantom touches tap the screen involuntarily
options.defect_description: Defective capacitive digitizer layer / electrostatic noise

leaf_diagnosis.title: Defective Touchscreen Digitizer (Ghost Touches)
leaf_diagnosis.issue: A warped screen bezel, hairline fracture in the capacitive ITO layer, or ungrounded AC charger is injecting false capacitive touch points.
remediation: Test unplugged on battery power to rule out noisy ground from a cheap third-party charger.
Recalibrate touch in Windows Tablet PC settings.
If hardware fault persists, disable 'HID-compliant touch screen' in Device Manager to preserve mouse usability.

q_stylus_pen.title: Active Stylus / Pen Input
q_stylus_pen.question: If using an active pen (Wacom/MPP), does it track smoothly with pressure sensitivity and zero jitter?
q_stylus_pen.why: Checks electromagnetic resonance (EMR) or active electrostatic (AES) digitizer controller.

options.label: Works smoothly (or no stylus used)
Erratic tracking, heavy line jitter, or no pressure sensitivity
options.defect_description: Stylus AAAA battery dead or worn pen tip

q_fingerprint_reader.title: Biometric Fingerprint Scanner
q_fingerprint_reader.question: Does the fingerprint sensor reliably log in with Windows Hello, or does it say 'Sensor unavailable'?
q_fingerprint_reader.why: Checks SPI/USB biometric daughterboard communication and Windows Biometric Framework.

options.label: Scans instantly and accurately (or laptop lacks sensor)
Fails to scan or shows yellow triangle 'Code 10' in Device Manager
options.defect_description: Biometric driver corruption or loose ribbon cable

q_sd_card_reader.title: SD / MicroSD Card Slot
q_sd_card_reader.question: When an SD card is inserted, does the laptop detect it and transfer files smoothly?
q_sd_card_reader.why: Validates PCIe/USB Realtek/Genesys card reader controller and spring-loaded card lock.

options.label: Reads and writes files properly (or laptop has no SD slot)
Card is not recognized or spring mechanism won't click-lock
options.defect_description: Bent card reader spring pin or disabled controller

q_ethernet_rj45.title: Wired RJ-45 Ethernet Port
q_ethernet_rj45.question: If your laptop has an RJ-45 Ethernet port, does it connect and establish Gigabit speeds with link lights?
q_ethernet_rj45.why: Validates physical magnetics and Realtek/Intel LAN PHY chip.

options.label: Connects instantly with solid link lights (or no RJ-45 port)
Port drop-jaw door is snapped or cable won't latch
options.defect_description: Broken plastic RJ-45 hinge jaw or damaged contact pin

q_thunderbolt_dock.title: Thunderbolt / Multi-Display Docking
q_thunderbolt_dock.question: When connecting an external USB-C / Thunderbolt dock, do displays, Ethernet, and USB hubs enumerate reliably?
q_thunderbolt_dock.why: Tests Intel Titan Ridge / Goshen Ridge Thunderbolt controller PCIe tunneling.

options.label: All dock functions enumerate smoothly (or no dock used)
Dock constantly disconnects, flickers displays, or drops USB
options.defect_description: Thunderbolt firmware handshake failure or loose port solder

q_gpu_mux_switch.title: Advanced Optimus / MUX Switch Transition
q_gpu_mux_switch.question: On gaming laptops with a MUX switch, does the display switch between iGPU and dGPU without black-screening?
q_gpu_mux_switch.why: Validates hardware display multiplexer IC routing eDP signals.

options.label: Switches seamlessly between integrated and dedicated graphics
Screen goes black permanently during GPU mode switch
options.defect_description: MUX switch handshake failure / display driver deadlock

leaf_diagnosis.title: Nvidia Advanced Optimus / MUX Switch Display Handshake Failure
leaf_diagnosis.issue: The hardware display multiplexer failed to hand over the eDP timing clock when switching display control between Intel/AMD iGPU and Nvidia dGPU.
remediation: Update both the integrated graphics driver and dedicated Nvidia driver to matching WHQL releases.
In BIOS, toggle graphics mode from 'Dynamic / Advanced Optimus' to 'Discrete Only' as a temporary workaround.
Update laptop OEM BIOS firmware for display MUX timing fixes.

q_audio_microphone_echo.title: Microphone Noise Cancellation & Echo
q_audio_microphone_echo.question: During calls (Zoom, Teams), do other people complain of loud buzzing, robot voice, or deafening background hiss?
q_audio_microphone_echo.why: Detects defective dual-array digital MEMS microphone capsules in the screen bezel.

options.label: Microphone audio is crisp and intelligible
Loud electrical hiss, screeching echo, or muffled audio
options.defect_description: Failing digital MEMS microphone or blocked pinhole port

q_lid_sensor_magnet.title: Lid Close / Sleep Sensor (Hall Effect)
q_lid_sensor_magnet.question: Does the laptop screen stay on when closed, or suddenly go to sleep while open if you rest your hands or a watch on the palm rest?
q_lid_sensor_magnet.why: Magnetic jewelry or failing Hall effect magnetic switches falsely trigger laptop sleep mode.

options.label: Sleeps properly when closed, stays awake when open
Sleeps unexpectedly while open or stays awake when lid is closed
options.defect_description: Misaligned Hall-effect magnetic lid switch or smart watch magnet interference

leaf_diagnosis.title: Hall Effect Magnetic Lid Sensor Misbehavior
leaf_diagnosis.issue: Laptops use a Hall effect sensor on the motherboard paired with a neodymium magnet in the screen bezel to detect when the lid is closed. Magnetic smartwatch bands or misplaced magnets trigger false sleep commands.
remediation: Remove magnetic Apple Watch / smartwatch bands or bracelets from your wrists while typing.
Inspect screen bezel top edge to verify the small magnet has not dislodged.
In Windows Power Options, set 'When I close the lid' to 'Do Nothing' to verify.

q_chassis_screws.title: Bottom Panel Screws & Rubber Feet
q_chassis_screws.question: Are all bottom chassis screws present and tight, and are the rubber elevation feet intact?
q_chassis_screws.why: Missing rubber feet choke bottom airflow intakes; missing screws cause motherboard PCB flex.

options.label: All screws and rubber feet are fully intact
Several screws are stripped/missing, or rubber feet are gone
options.defect_description: Missing bottom panel screws or rubber airflow risers
